newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
STRONG TEAM FOR ADMIRAL'S CUP

Australia returns to the Admiral's Cup scene in England with a strong team again headed by Sydney businessman and international yachtsman SYD FISCHER whose team in 1993 came within a quarter of a point of victory.
Admiral's Cup teams this year will comprise a Mumm 36 one-design, an ILC40 and a big boat, an IMS handicap yacht in the 44-55 ft LOA range and between 550.0 and 510.0 second per mile GPH.

FISCHER, who has been appointed team captain, will campaign the big boat of the team, which will be either his highly successful current Farr 50, Ragamuffin, or another yacht more suitable to the lighter conditions normally experienced out of Cowes and in the English Channel in mid-summer.

FISCHER, boss of the Gazebo Hotel, is still Australia's most successful ocean racing campaigner and was recently named Australian Ocean Racer of the Year for 1996 following his success in leading Australian teams to victory in the Southern Cross Cup and Kenwood Cup.

Advertising man and highly successful ocean racing helmsman STEVE KULMAR will skipper a chartered Mumm 36 in a campaign that will include the Mumm 36 world championships in the lead-up to the Admiral's Cup, which starts on July 31 and ends with the Fastnet Race, starting August 9.

The ILC40 in the Australian team will be the impressive Farr-designed G Net, which has been chartered from its Japanese owner by a syndicate put together by North Sails director GRANT SIMMER and headed by Melbourne merchant banker JOHN CALVERT-JONES.
DAVID KELLETT, chairman of the Australian Yachting Federation's Offshore Committee, today described the team as an excellent team with a very professional approach.

The Australian team of Ragamuffin, Great News II and Ninja lost by a mere 0.25 of a point to Germany in the 1993 Admiral's Cup, but we were not represented at Cowes in 1995 other than by ANDREW STRACHAN's Ninety Seven in the Hong Kong team.
AUSSIES FOURTH AT KEY WEST REGATTA
As part of his preparation for the Admiral's Cup, STEVE KULMAR chartered the U.S. Mumm 36, Fast Tango, for the 1997 Yachting Key West Race Week which ended last weekend.
Although just an average boat, Fast Tango was sailed exceptionally well by KULMAR and his crew which included Admiral's Cup campaign partner RICHARD FREIDRICHS and tactician RON JACOBS.

The Australians won the third race and finished fourth overall in the eight heat event against highly professional crews from the USA, Japan, France, England and Brazil. The Brazilians including Brazil's two Olympic gold medallists, TORBEN GRAEL (Star) and ROBERT SCHEIDT (Laser).
KULMAR won the owner/driver award for the regatta. The Aussies also teamed up with a New Zealand crew racing a Melges 24 to form a Down Under Team for the regatta, finishing second overall.

Attracting some 280 yachts, Key West Race Week is a showcase of American yacht design, with the latest IMS boats competing along with a strong one-design fleet that included ID 48s, Corel 45s, Mumm 36s, Mumm 30s, J80s, J27s and sixty Melges 24s.
SAIL FOR CANCER RESEARCH

For the past 12 years, NSW sailors, corporations and generous individuals have come to the support of the Sail for Cancer Research, raising A$1.13 million for the Jenny & Leo Foundation and its community-funded leukaemia and cancer research.
The event has now gone far beyond the Sail for Cancer day on Sydney Harbour, with events planned for Sunday, February 23 on the Harbour, Pittwater, Port Hacking and Botany Bay.

The Foundation is still looking for yachts and other pleasure craft to take part, which includes taking guests, and entry forms are available from the Cruising Yacht Club, Middle Harbour Yacht Club, Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club and Cronulla Sailing Club or from JANE at the Foundation on 02/9371-0400.
INTERESTED IN SPEED?
The fastest man on water, KEN WARBY, will be at the Australian Maritime Museum next Wednesday evening, February 12, to talk about his new attempt to raise his own speed record.

Despite several attempts, nobody has beaten WARBY's amazing world water speed record 511 km/hr which he set with his hydroplane Spirit of Australia on Blowering Dam, NSW in 1978. Next year, 20 years later, he will return to the water in a boat to try and set a new world mark.
The talk is free, starting at 6pm, but phone 9552-755 to reserve your seats. You will also be able to see WARBY's original Spirit of Australia, now permanently displayed at the Maritime Museum.
CHAMPION OF THE SKIFFS

The Sydney Olympics may still be a long way down the track, but former Lake Macquarie sailor CHRIS NICHOLSON is already being spoken of as Australia's best prospect for a gold medal in the new 49-er high performance skiff class.
Certainly, if his determination and sailing ability shown in last weekend's Oracle Grand Prix Series for 18-footers is any criteria he has a head start into the new Olympic class.

NICHOLSON, a former world champion in the International 505 dinghy class, dominated the Grand Prix Series, winning regattas in Brisbane, Auckland and Adelaide and then the final regatta on Sydney Harbour.

However, he and his crew of DANIEL PHILLIPS and GARY BOYD had to fight back to win the Sydney series from Prudential, skippered by the evergreen ROB BROWN who celebrated his 42nd birthday last Sunday.
With the Grand Prix series over, NICHOLSON will soon take delivery of his new 49-er and begin an Olympic campaign starting with the Sail Sydney 97 Regatta on the Harbour at Easter.
WHAT'S COMING UP IN YACHTING

FEBRUARY 9: BT Global Challenge sprint leg to Sydney starts from Wellington, New Zealand. Britain's Prince Michael of Kent will be sailing aboard Ocean Rover, one of 14 one-design 60-footers competing in this race around the world the wrong way .

FEBRUARY 15: Most of the BT Global Challenge fleet expected to reach Sydney, with the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia finishing them off the Opera House. They will berth at the Australian Maritime Museum, Darling Harbour, before heading for Cape Town on March 4.
FEBRUARY 9-14: WOW Nortel Asia Pacific Women's Regatta, run by the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron on the Harbour, sailing J24s and Elliott 5.9 sports boats (for crews under 25).
FEBRUARY 14-16: Cruising Yacht Club's Wollongong Weekend, with overnight race starting 2000 hours on Friday; return race starting off historic Flagstaff Point on the Sunday morning.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
